issues.title: Mention hybrid algorithms
issues.author: clementpapon
issues.body:
> Originally reported at https://github.com/gselander/pq-suites/issues/3, by @emanjon on 11 June 2026.

Discussed today during LAKE DT meeting.

Draft should mention that hybrid algorithms could be registered in the future.

comments.author: clementpapon
comments.body:
From Lidia Pocero Fraile on 3 July 2026:

https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/lake/D5r0X-GKUyQ-X4k8PtJow3rYFxA/

As a possible suggestion for future consideration, I think the draft could also benefit from including PQ/T hybrid KEM cipher suites. Section 3 already states that “KEM applies both to standalone KEMs and hybrid KEMs,” and I think this could be directly leveraged to provide protection against Harvest Now, Decrypt Later (HNDL) attacks simply by defining a cipher suite that includes a hybrid KEM.

comments.author: emanjon
comments.body:
I would prefer to not have to register new COSE algorithms, and do as LAKE have done in the past. We would prefer to wait for COSE to register KEMs that we can use.

An alternative would be to hybridise on the protocol level like TLS, but that would require a sepearate draft and new formal verification.

I think we should just add that

```
"PQ/T hybrid algorithms such as [X] could be registered in the future."

[X] draft-irtf-cfrg-concrete-hybrid-kems

```

issues.title: Clément's review
issues.author: clementpapon
issues.body:
> Originally reported at https://github.com/gselander/pq-suites/issues/8, by @gselander on 16 July 2026.

https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/lake/BH2ugEAuLOiVPVeV5zbNMnXWh78/

Section 2: The document should maybe clarify that SHA-256 remains available at the application layer, for consistency with the cipher suites proposed in Section 6.2.

Section 3: Minor correction on the KEM definition (K = decaps (sk, c)). A paragraph should maybe be added clarifying that G_X follows the same behaviour as G_Y, and stating the impact of PQ algorithm on key and signature sizes.

Section 4: In my opinion, this section should be significantly expanded to cover the properties preserved by the transition to a KEM-based key exchange, with references to existing formal analysis results (in particular, the formal verification of EDHOC-PSK with KEM, and also Jacomme et al. analysis of EDHOC Method 0 with a KEM (« A comprehensive, formal and automated analysis of the EDHOC protocol »). The section should also explicitly state that these cipher suites provide protection against Store-Now Decrypt-Later (SNDL) attacks.

Section 6.1: Perhaps the draft could anticipate the arrival of EDHOC-PSK and suggest an additional line for PSK mode, similar to Value: 0.

Section 6.2: For cipher suite 3, there is an error: according to IANA, we have ML-DSA-87 (not 85) and -50 (not -48). A paragraph should maybe be added stating that ML-DSA and ML-KEM are the most interesting algorithms to implement currently, but there is a counterpart with their larger key and signature sizes that may preclude their use on the most constrained device classes (e.g., Class 0/C0 devices).

Also, perhaps a more delicate point to raise about cipher suite negotiation: if the Initiator supports PQ but the Responder does not, I think this follows the standard EDHOC fallback mechanism. However, this scenario may affect the Identity Protection property and deserves explicit discussion in the Security Considerations section in my opinion.

comments.author: clementpapon
comments.body: Some suggestions regarding these comments. Section 4 will probably need to be expanded. This is PR https://github.com/lake-wg/pqsuites/pull/8.

issues.title: New notation for G_X, G_Y?
issues.author: gselander
issues.body:
RFC9528 uses G_X and G_Y for DH keys. This notation does not map well when DH is replaced by KEM. We also want to cover potential future NIKE. Should we change notation? 

To what? After discussion with GPT-5.4 mini we agreed on "key contribution".

G_X := KC_I = key contribution of Initiator
G_Y := KC_R = key contribution of Responder

comments.author: gselander
comments.body:
Alternatively "key share"

G_X := KS_I = key share of Initiator
G_Y := KS_R = key share of Responder

comments.author: gselander
comments.body:
Also may want to rename the message_2 field:
G_Y_CIPHERTEXT_2 := KI_R_CIPHERTEXT_2, etc.

and Shared Secret:
G_XY := SS

comments.author: gselander
comments.body: This is not targeting retroactive updates, just to have a common terminology in current drafts and going forward.

issues.title: What is "DH/NIKE"?
issues.author: cabo
issues.body:
ChatGPT had this definition:

> In sneaker circles, “DH/Nike” usually refers to fake Nike shoes bought from DHgate.

I'm sure something else is meant, but that should be defined as a term (beyond just expanding the abbreviations, which doesn't help with the undefined meaning of the slash construction).
